stories.headline: Anthropic Restores Third-Party Agent Access With New Agent SDK Credits Starting June 15

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Anthropic announced a new 'Agent SDK' credit category for paid Claude subscribers, reversing its April 2026 policy that had barred third-party agents like OpenClaw from running on Claude subscriptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced via its official developer communications account on X, @ClaudeDevs, that it is changing its Claude paid subscription tiers, introducing a new subcategory of 'Agent SDK' credits for all paid subscribers, which they can now allocate specifically for 'programmatic' uses, including external, third-party agents such as OpenClaw.

key_facts.fact: Starting June 15, 2026, Claude Agent SDK and `claude -p` usage will no longer count toward a plan's regular usage limits; eligible Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users instead claim a separate monthly credit.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting June 15, 2026, Claude Agent SDK and `claude -p` usage no longer counts toward your Claude plan's usage limits. Your subscription usage limits stay the same and stay reserved for interactive use of Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and Claude.

key_facts.fact: Monthly Agent SDK credit amounts are $20 for Pro, $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, $20 for Team Standard seats, $100 for Team Premium seats, and $20 to $200 for Enterprise plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Pro $20 | Max 5x $100 | Max 20x $200 | Team (Standard seats) $20 | Team (Premium seats) $100 | Enterprise (usage-based) $20 | Enterprise (seat-based Premium seats) $200

key_facts.fact: The credit covers the Agent SDK, the `claude -p` non-interactive command, the Claude Code GitHub Actions integration, and third-party apps that authenticate with a Claude subscription; API key users are unaffected and keep pay-as-you-go billing.
key_facts.excerpt: The Agent SDK monthly credit applies to: The `claude -p` command in Claude Code (non-interactive mode); The Claude Code GitHub Actions integration; Third-party apps that authenticate with your Claude subscription through the Agent SDK.

key_facts.fact: The April 2026 prohibition was introduced after some subscribers paying $20 to $200 per month consumed hundreds or thousands of dollars of tokens through OpenClaw and similar autonomous agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Some Claude subscribers were paying $20 to $200 per month under Anthropic's Claude Pro and Max subscriptions, but consuming hundreds, even thousands of dollars of tokens above those prices through their OpenClaw (and similar autonomous) agents. This was an unsustainable position for Anthropic's finances and its limited compute infrastructure.

stories.headline: Claude Mythos Preview Becomes First AI to Complete Both of UK AISI's Cyber Ranges

key_facts.fact: A newer Claude Mythos Preview checkpoint became the first AI model to complete both of the UK AI Security Institute's cyber ranges, which simulate cyberattacks on small, undefended enterprise networks.
key_facts.excerpt: In AISI's latest testing, the newer Mythos Preview checkpoint completed both our cyber ranges... This was the first time that a model completed the second of our two cyber ranges.

key_facts.fact: The checkpoint solved the 32-step corporate network attack range 'The Last Ones' in 6 of 10 attempts and the previously unsolved operational-technology range 'Cooling Tower' in 3 of 10 attempts.
key_facts.excerpt: The newer Mythos Preview checkpoint completed both our cyber ranges, solving the range 'The Last Ones' in 6 of 10 attempts and the previously unsolved 'Cooling Tower' in 3 of 10 attempts.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's GPT-5.5 solved 'The Last Ones' in 3 of 10 attempts and did not complete 'Cooling Tower'.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.5 solved 'The Last Ones' on 3 of 10 attempts.

key_facts.fact: AISI estimated in February 2026 that the length of cyber tasks frontier models can complete had been doubling every 4.7 months since late 2024, down from an 8-month estimate in November 2025; Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5 substantially exceeded both trends.
key_facts.excerpt: In February 2026, we internally estimated that the length of cyber tasks AI models could complete had doubled every 4.7 months since late 2024 – already an acceleration from our November 2025 estimate of 8 months. Since then, AISI reported on two new models, Claude Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5, which substantially exceeded both doubling rate trends.

key_facts.fact: AISI's cyber range experiments give each model a budget of up to 100 million tokens per attempt, and recent models disproportionately benefit from higher token limits.
key_facts.excerpt: In our cyber range experiment we use up to 100M tokens and find performance would likely still improve beyond that budget, especially for recent models, which disproportionately benefit from higher token limits.

sources.title: How fast is autonomous AI cyber capability advancing?

stories.headline: Adaption Launches AutoScientist, an AI Tool That Automates the Model-Training Research Loop

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Adaption introduced AutoScientist, a system that automates the full research loop behind model training and alignment by co-optimizing training data and model recipes until quality converges on the user's objective.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're introducing AutoScientist, a system that self-improves and automates the full research loop behind model training and alignment. AutoScientist co-optimizes your data and model training recipes automatically, self-improving across both until quality converges on your objective.

key_facts.fact: CEO Sara Hooker, formerly VP of AI research at Cohere, said the tool co-optimizes both data and model and 'suggests we can finally allow for successful frontier AI trainings outside of these labs.'
key_facts.excerpt: “What's super exciting about it is that it co-optimizes both the data and the model, and learns the best way to basically learn any capability,” Hooker told TechCrunch. “It suggests we can finally allow for successful frontier AI trainings outside of these labs.”

key_facts.fact: Adaption says AutoScientist more than doubled win-rates across different models, with aggregate win-rate rising from 48% to 64% when AutoScientist was used instead of an AI researcher's recommendation.
key_facts.excerpt: In aggregate, win [rate moved from] 48% to 64% when AutoScientist was used instead of the AI researcher recommendation.

key_facts.fact: AutoScientist builds on Adaption's existing Adaptive Data product and is being offered free for the first 30 days after release; conventional benchmarks like SWE-Bench or ARC-AGI do not apply because the system adapts models to specific tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the system is built to adapt models to specific tasks, conventional benchmarks like SWE-Bench or ARC-AGI aren't applicable... the lab is making the tool free to use for the first 30 days after its release.

sources.title: Adaption aims big with AutoScientist, an AI tool that helps models train themselves

stories.headline: Rivian CEO's Mind Robotics Raises $400M Led by Kleiner Perkins for AI Manufacturing Robots

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Mind Robotics announced a $400 million financing led by Kleiner Perkins, bringing total investment in the company to more than $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Mind Robotics today announced a $400 million financing led by Kleiner Perkins, bringing total investment in Mind Robotics to more than $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: New investors include Meritech Capital, Redpoint Ventures, SV Angel, Incharge Capital, A-Star Capital and Garuda Ventures, alongside existing investors Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Eclipse, Prysm Capital, Bain Capital Ventures and Greenoaks.
key_facts.excerpt: This financing included participation from new investors including Meritech Capital, Redpoint Ventures, SV Angel, Incharge Capital, A-Star Capital, and Garuda Ventures as well as existing investors including Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Eclipse, Prysm Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and Greenoaks.

key_facts.fact: The round follows a $115 million seed financing in late 2025 and a $500 million Series A in March 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: This follows a seed financing of $115M in late 2025 and a Series A of $500M in March 2026.

key_facts.fact: Mind Robotics, founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe, builds AI-powered robots for manufacturing tasks and raised the round at a $3.4 billion valuation, according to a source.
key_facts.excerpt: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe's Mind Robotics, which is building AI-powered robots for manufacturing tasks, raised $400M, a source says at a $3.4B valuation.

stories.headline: Anthropic on Track for $50B Revenue Run Rate; Overtakes OpenAI in Business Adoption

key_facts.fact: Investor documents show Anthropic's revenue run rate is on track to hit $50 billion by the end of June, up sharply from an original full-year target of about $30 billion ARR.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's revenue run rate is on track to hit $50B by the end of June; Ramp says more of its customers now use Anthropic than OpenAI, a first.

key_facts.fact: Spend-management firm Ramp says more of its customers now use Anthropic than OpenAI, the first time Anthropic has led in business adoption.
key_facts.excerpt: Ramp says more of its customers now use Anthropic than OpenAI, a first.

key_facts.fact: The May Ramp AI Index put business adoption at 34.4% for Anthropic versus 32.3% for OpenAI, with OpenAI losing 2.9 points and Anthropic gaining 3.8 points in April while the total market grew just 0.2 points.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic just passed OpenAI in business AI adoption. 34.4% vs 32.3% per the May Ramp AI Index. OpenAI lost 2.9 points in April. Anthropic gained 3.8. The total market only grew 0.2.

sources.title: Anthropic Was Behind. Now It's the AI Boom's Front-Runner

stories.headline: Cerebras Prices IPO at $185, Above Range, Raising $5.55B in 2026's Biggest US Debut

key_facts.fact: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems priced its US IPO at $185 per share on May 13, above the marketed $150 to $160 range, selling 30 million shares to raise $5.55 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras Systems priced its U.S. initial public offering at $185 per share on Wednesday, above the top end of its indicated price range... The IPO raised $5.55 billion for Cerebras, based on 30 million shares sold.

key_facts.fact: The pricing implies a fully diluted valuation of about $56.43 billion, making it the largest stock market debut so far in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: It implies a valuation on Cerebras on a fully diluted basis of $56.43 billion, making it the largest stock market debut so far this year.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras had originally marketed the offering at $115 to $125 per share before revising the range to $150 to $160 and raising the share count from 28 million to 30 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The company marketed the offering at between $150 and $160 per share, up from an earlier range of $115 to $125 per share. It also increased the number of shares on offer to 30 million from 28 million.

key_facts.fact: Shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker 'CBRS' on May 14, with underwriters granted a 30-day option to buy up to 4.5 million additional shares.
key_facts.excerpt: The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on May 14, 2026, under the ticker symbol “CBRS.” ... Cerebras has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 4,500,000 shares.

stories.headline: Microsoft in Talks to Acquire Diffusion-LLM Startup Inception as It Hedges Against OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on May 13, citing five sources, that Microsoft has been quietly canvassing AI startups for acquisitions or strategic deals to build the option to operate independently of OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing five people familiar with the matter, that the company has been quietly canvassing AI startups for acquisitions or strategic deals as it builds out the option to operate without OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is in active talks with Inception, a Palo Alto startup spun out of Stanford by professor Stefano Ermon that builds diffusion-based language models processing tokens in parallel rather than one at a time.
key_facts.excerpt: The active conversation now is with Inception, a Palo Alto startup spun out of Stanford by professor Stefano Ermon. Inception is one of the very few groups outside the major labs building diffusion-based language models rather than autoregressive ones.

key_facts.fact: Inception is seeking an acquisition price of more than $1 billion, and SpaceX has also courted the startup.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft has discussed deal with AI startup Inception: sources... Inception, which is looking for a price of over $1B.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's M12 fund participated in Inception's $50 million round last November; earlier this spring Microsoft weighed acquiring Cursor but backed away over antitrust concerns tied to its ownership of GitHub Copilot.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft's M12 fund already participated in the company's $50m round last November... Cursor was the first try and fell apart over GitHub Copilot.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's MAI Superintelligence team, set up in November 2025 under Mustafa Suleyman, shipped its first three foundation models in April, with a frontier general-purpose LLM targeted for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The MAI Superintelligence team, set up in November 2025 under Mustafa Suleyman, shipped its first three foundation models in April: MAI-Transcribe-1, MAI-Voice-1, and MAI-Image-2. A frontier general-purpose LLM is, per Suleyman's own March memo, the 2027 target.
